name: CNY17-2
title: CNY17 family (CNY17-1 to CNY17-4): phototransistor optocoupler with base pin, 5000 Vrms, DIP-6 and SMD-6
summary: A single-channel optocoupler: an infrared GaAs LED facing a silicon NPN phototransistor whose base is brought out. It is sold in four current-transfer-ratio bins, -1 to -4, spanning 40 % to 320 % at IF = 10 mA; the CNY17-2 is the 63 % to 125 % bin. The collector-emitter rating is 70 V and the isolation test voltage 5000 Vrms for one minute. Packages are the standard 7.62 mm DIP-6, a 10.16 mm wide-lead DIP-6 (option 6) and two surface-mount forms (options 7 and 9), with or without VDE approval.

circuits.description: A current pulse from a 50 Ω generator drives the LED; the LED current returns to ground through a 50 Ω resistor whose voltage channel I shows. The phototransistor collector sits on +5 V and its emitter drives the load RL to ground, which channel II shows. The base is left open.

equations.name: Current transfer ratio
equations.note: Graded into four bins at VCE = 5 V, IF = 10 mA.

operation.text: One gallium arsenide infrared LED shines on a silicon NPN phototransistor inside a six-pin dual-in-line body. The transistor base comes out on pin 6. The coupler carries signals down to DC across an isolation barrier tested at 5000 Vrms for one minute. Typical uses: relay and transformer replacement in digital interfaces, and analog signal paths such as CRT modulation.

The four parts are sorted by current transfer ratio at IF = 10 mA and VCE = 5 V: CNY17-1 40 % to 80 %, CNY17-2 63 % to 125 %, CNY17-3 100 % to 200 %, CNY17-4 160 % to 320 %. At IF = 1 mA the ratio is lower, with minimums of 13, 22, 34 and 56 %. The two higher bins also have the higher dark current limit (100 nA against 50 nA at VCE = 10 V). In the saturated switching figures each bin is driven at its own LED current: 20 mA for -1, 10 mA for -2 and -3, 5 mA for -4.

Normalized to IF = 10 mA at 25 °C, the transfer ratio peaks near 10 mA to 15 mA and falls on both sides; at 1 mA it is about half of the 10 mA figure at 25 °C. It peaks near 0 °C and drops to about 0.76 at -55 °C and 0.64 at 110 °C. Saturated (VCE = 0.4 V) and non-saturated (VCE = 5 V) curves are close to each other.

Times are measured on the collector-current pulse against the LED pulse. Delay runs until the current starts to rise, rise time is from 10 % to 90 %, storage time lasts until it starts to fall and fall time is from 90 % to 10 %. Turn-on is delay plus rise; turn-off is storage plus fall. With a 75 Ω load the transistor stays linear and both turn-on and turn-off are about 2 µs to 3 µs; in saturation turn-off stretches to 18 µs to 25 µs. Turn-off time grows steeply with load resistance, to about 170 µs at 20 kΩ.
The LED may dissipate 100 mW, the phototransistor 150 mW and the whole coupler 250 mW up to 25 °C ambient. Above 25 °C each limit falls linearly to about 15 mW, 20 mW and 30 mW at 110 °C.

All versions are covered by the safety model number CNY17. Approvals: UL file E52744; cUL to CSA 22.2 bulletin 5A; DIN EN 60747-5-5 (VDE 0884-5); BSI to IEC 60950 and IEC 60065; FIMKO to EN60950; CQC to GB8898-2011. VDE approval applies to the option 1, 16, 17 and 19 order codes. The part is lead-free and RoHS compliant.

The top carries the base part number (for example CNY17-3), the UL mark, and a code line of the form V YWW followed by a two-digit code; pin 1 is marked at one corner. The VDE mark appears only on option 1 parts. Neither the packaging option nor the T suffix is marked.
